F1.quote: Worker Info Exchange | Data Rights for Digital Workers | London
F1.claim: the entity's own page names it for data rights for digital workers, in London
F1.lineage: where and under what name: London, digital workers

F2.quote: Worker Info Exchange is a non-profit helping workers reclaim control over the data collected from them at work. We help workers turn data into power — challenging unfair algorithmic systems and holding tech platforms to account.
F2.claim: Worker Info Exchange defined by itself: a non-profit helping workers reclaim control over the data collected from them at work, turning data into power, challenging unfair algorithmic systems and holding tech platforms to account
F2.lineage: what it is: a non-profit helping workers turn the data collected from them at work into power

F3.quote: Stichting WIE International has launched a new collective action against Uber over its unfair dynamic pay system to stop algorithmic wage cuts and secure compensation for the damages drivers have suffered.
F3.claim: Stichting WIE International has launched a collective action against Uber over its dynamic pay system, to stop algorithmic wage cuts and secure compensation
F3.lineage: the Uber collective action: the Dynamic Pay Claim

F4.quote: Opaque automated management systems foster exploitation and discrimination. We challenge these practices through three strands of activity
F4.claim: opaque automated management systems foster exploitation and discrimination; it challenges them through three strands of activity
F4.lineage: the problem it names: workers managed by hidden algorithms

F5.quote: We facilitate data access by making specific subject access and data portability requests on behalf of workers. Our goal is to create transparency over their working conditions by interrogating how their work is allocated, how their pay is determined and how their performance is assessed.
F5.claim: its first strand: subject access and data portability requests made on behalf of workers, to create transparency over how their work is allocated, how their pay is determined and how their performance is assessed
F5.lineage: the three strands: data access, data investigations, data trusts

F6.quote: We carry out targeted investigations and data analyses to expose unfair algorithmic decision making. These investigations support the strategic litigation work through which we help workers contest illegal automated dismissals and management decisions.
F6.claim: its second strand: targeted investigations and data analyses exposing unfair algorithmic decision making, supporting strategic litigation against illegal automated dismissals and management decisions
F6.lineage: the three strands: data access, data investigations, data trusts

F7.quote: We support trade unions and grassroots worker organisations to aggregate their data with other workers through the development of data trusts. Armed with powerful analysis, workers can be better resourced for collective bargaining and action.
F7.claim: its third strand: supporting trade unions and grassroots worker organisations to aggregate their data through data trusts, for collective bargaining and action
F7.lineage: the three strands: data access, data investigations, data trusts

F8.quote: Managed by Bots Report Just Eat Report McMisery Report Dying for Data Report Workers' Recommendations on EU Directive
F8.claim: its research reports: Managed by Bots, Just Eat, McMisery, Dying for Data, and Workers' Recommendations on the EU Directive
F8.lineage: reports and news on its own site

F9.quote: Liverpool Uber drivers hit by falling pay and soaring commission fees as AI controlled "dynamic pay" takes hold Worker Info Exchange Jul 23
F9.claim: its latest news item (dated Jul 23, no year shown): Liverpool Uber drivers hit by falling pay and soaring commission fees as AI-controlled dynamic pay takes hold
F9.lineage: dynamic pay: what changed for drivers

F10.quote: Drivers in UK and Europe set to sue Uber for unfair pay set by algorithm Worker Info Exchange Nov 20, 2025
F10.claim: news, 20 November 2025: drivers in the UK and Europe set to sue Uber for unfair pay set by algorithm
F10.lineage: the Uber collective action: the Dynamic Pay Claim

F11.quote: New Research Exposes Deepening Exploitation of Uber Drivers by Algorithmic Pay Worker Info Exchange Jun 19, 2025
F11.claim: news, 19 June 2025: new research exposing deepening exploitation of Uber drivers by algorithmic pay
F11.lineage: research: the Oxford audit and the TUC report

F13.quote: Worker Info Exchange's Equivalency Determination (ED) is certified by NGOsource.
F13.claim: its equivalency determination is certified by NGOsource

F14.quote: The platform economy is sold as a story of freedom, yet hidden algorithms decide who works, who waits, and who earns.
F14.claim: the platform economy is sold as freedom while hidden algorithms decide who works, who waits and who earns
F14.lineage: the problem it names: workers managed by hidden algorithms

F15.quote: Stichting WIE International holds platforms to account and defends the rights of gig workers in the Netherlands, the UK, and Europe.
F15.claim: Stichting WIE International defined by itself: it holds platforms to account and defends gig workers' rights in the Netherlands, the UK and Europe
F15.lineage: the foundation: Stichting WIE International, in cooperation with WIE

F16.quote: From 2020, Uber quietly started making changes to its systems to make driver pay dynamic.
F16.claim: from 2020 Uber began changing its systems to make driver pay dynamic
F16.lineage: dynamic pay: what changed for drivers

F17.quote: Behind the promise of “fairer” pricing, this system quietly shifted risk onto drivers while enabling Uber to increase its hidden commission — in some cases taking nearly half of the fare.
F17.claim: dynamic pay shifted risk onto drivers and let Uber increase its hidden commission, in some cases to nearly half the fare
F17.lineage: dynamic pay: what changed for drivers

F18.quote: Before the introduction of Dynamic Pay, driver earnings were calculated transparently, based on fixed per-minute and per-kilometer/mile rates, with Uber’s commission set at 25%.
F18.claim: before dynamic pay, earnings were calculated from fixed per-minute and per-distance rates with a 25% commission
F18.lineage: dynamic pay: what changed for drivers

F19.quote: After the introduction of Dynamic Pay, driver pay and work allocation became variable, non-transparent and determined in real time by Uber’s algorithm.
F19.claim: after dynamic pay, driver pay and work allocation became variable, non-transparent and set in real time by Uber's algorithm
F19.lineage: dynamic pay: what changed for drivers

F20.quote: Research by Oxford University and Worker Info Exchange, based on 1.5 million trips, shows falling driver pay, increased unpaid waiting time, and growing inequality, with most drivers earning less while Uber profits more.
F20.claim: research by Oxford University and Worker Info Exchange on 1.5 million trips shows falling pay, more unpaid waiting time and growing inequality, most drivers earning less while Uber profits more
F20.lineage: research: the Oxford audit and the TUC report

F21.quote: Stichting WIE International has launched the Dynamic Pay Claim under Dutch WAMCA law to challenge this system, expose its impact, and seek remedies for affected drivers.
F21.claim: Stichting WIE International brings the Dynamic Pay Claim under the Dutch WAMCA law
F21.lineage: the Uber collective action: the Dynamic Pay Claim

F22.quote: The foundation also wants to enforce transparency regarding the use and training of the underlying algorithms as well as secure compensation for drivers who have suffered damages as a result of Dynamic Pay.
F22.claim: the claim seeks transparency on the use and training of the algorithms and compensation for drivers' damages
F22.lineage: the Uber collective action: the Dynamic Pay Claim

F23.quote: Stichting WIE International is also fighting for drivers whose personal data was unlawfully transferred to the United States by Uber between 2021 and September 2023.
F23.claim: the foundation also acts for drivers whose personal data Uber unlawfully transferred to the United States between 2021 and September 2023
F23.lineage: the Uber collective action: the Dynamic Pay Claim

F24.quote: At the moment, Stichting WIE International is focusing on drivers from the Netherlands, Belgium, France, Germany, Poland, Romania and the United Kingdom who have driven for Uber at any time after November 2020.
F24.claim: the claim covers drivers from seven countries who drove for Uber after November 2020
F24.lineage: the Uber collective action: the Dynamic Pay Claim

F25.quote: There are no upfront fees for drivers — case costs are covered by third-party funding.
F25.claim: no upfront fees; costs covered by third-party funding
F25.lineage: the Uber collective action: the Dynamic Pay Claim

F26.quote: Stichting WIE International, a Dutch foundation working in cooperation with Worker Info Exchange, empowers gig workers to fight back with their data against platform service providers.
F26.claim: Stichting WIE International is a Dutch foundation working in cooperation with Worker Info Exchange (two bodies)
F26.lineage: the foundation: Stichting WIE International, in cooperation with WIE

F27.quote: Access their rights under the GDPR to request and understand their data … Expose unfair practices through participatory research and audits … Advocate for systemic change with trade unions, policymakers, and courts … Obtain compensation for workers to make up for inflicted harm
F27.claim: the foundation's four aims: GDPR data access, participatory research and audits, advocacy with unions, policymakers and courts, compensation
F27.lineage: the foundation: Stichting WIE International, in cooperation with WIE

F28.quote: We partner with leading universities and worker groups to audit platform algorithms. Our studies have revealed falling pay, rising inequality, and a lack of transparency in the gig economy.
F28.claim: it partners with universities and worker groups to audit platform algorithms; its studies found falling pay, rising inequality and opacity
F28.lineage: research: the Oxford audit and the TUC report

F29.quote: Through workshops and legal support, we equip workers to use their own data to demand transparency and accountability.
F29.claim: workshops and legal support equip workers to use their own data
F29.lineage: the foundation: Stichting WIE International, in cooperation with WIE

F30.quote: Worker Info Exchange partners with TUC on “landmark” new reportexposing the human cost of Uber’s dynamic pay … April 29, 2026
F30.claim: 29 April 2026: Worker Info Exchange partners with the TUC on a report on the human cost of Uber's dynamic pay
F30.lineage: research: the Oxford audit and the TUC report

F31.quote: Worker Info Exchange (WIE), a non‑profit organisation turning worker data into collective power , has today welcomed the TUC’s new report, The Human Price of Dynamic Pay , as a landmark investigation into the impact of algorithmic pay systems on drivers’ lives.
F31.claim: WIE welcomed the TUC's report The Human Price of Dynamic Pay as a landmark investigation of algorithmic pay
F31.lineage: research: the Oxford audit and the TUC report

F32.quote: WIE was research partner with the TUC on the project to document how Uber’s move to dynamic pay has deepened insecurity across the ride‑hail and delivery economy.
F32.claim: WIE was the TUC's research partner on the project
F32.lineage: research: the Oxford audit and the TUC report

F33.quote: The report draws on powerful first-hand testimony from eleven Uber and delivery drivers who describe how the company’s “dynamic pay” system, a constantly shifting, algorithmic model that determines how much workers earn on each job, has eroded income stability, increased unpaid hours, and worsened mental and physical health.
F33.claim: the report rests on the testimony of eleven drivers: dynamic pay eroded income stability, increased unpaid hours and worsened health
F33.lineage: research: the Oxford audit and the TUC report

F34.quote: WIE, through its Dynamic Pay campaign , is currently coordinating a collective legal action against Uber in the Dutch courts, arguing that the company’s dynamic pricing systems breach drivers’ data protection and transparency rights under EU law.
F34.claim: WIE, through its Dynamic Pay campaign, is coordinating the collective legal action against Uber in the Dutch courts
F34.lineage: the Uber collective action: the Dynamic Pay Claim

F35.quote: James Farrar, Director of WIE, comments … That dynamic pay is not innovation, it’s exploitation by algorithm, a business model built on secrecy and unequal power.
F35.claim: its Director, James Farrar: dynamic pay is exploitation by algorithm, built on secrecy and unequal power
F35.lineage: dynamic pay: what changed for drivers

F36.quote: Cansu Safak, Research Lead at WIE, comments … a decline in wages that our earlier participatory audit with Oxford University, built from drivers’ own data subject access requests, had already exposed in numbers.
F36.claim: its Research Lead, Cansu Safak: the earlier participatory audit with Oxford University was built from drivers' own data subject access requests
F36.lineage: research: the Oxford audit and the TUC report

F37.quote: With no transparency over the conditions they work under, drivers have been forced to turn to data protection law as the only remaining route to assert their rights.
F37.claim: Safak: data protection law is drivers' only remaining route to assert their rights
F37.lineage: the route: workers' digital rights under the law

F38.quote: We need enforcement rather than reform. Drivers are already workers, but government has no appetite for enforcing the law.
F38.claim: its position: drivers are already workers; enforcement, not reform
F38.lineage: the route: workers' digital rights under the law

F39.quote: WIE argues that Uber’s use of algorithmically set dynamic pay is unlawful under Article 22 of the EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), which gives drivers the right not to be subject to decisions based solely on automated decision-making, including profiling.
F39.claim: WIE argues dynamic pay is unlawful under GDPR Article 22, the right not to be subject to solely automated decisions
F39.lineage: the Uber collective action: the Dynamic Pay Claim

F40.quote: Uber is also not transparent about how its algorithm works, and has used drivers’ own historical data to train the system that now determines their pay.
F40.claim: Uber trained the pay system on drivers' own historical data, without transparency
F40.lineage: dynamic pay: what changed for drivers

F41.quote: Separately, Uber has already been fined for unlawfully transferring driver data to the United States between August 2021 and September 2023.
F41.claim: Uber was fined for unlawfully transferring driver data to the United States, August 2021 to September 2023
F41.lineage: the Uber collective action: the Dynamic Pay Claim

F42.quote: Joint analysis by Oxford University and WIE , covering 1.5 million Uber trips between 2016 and 2024, found that after the introduction of dynamic pricing in 2023, drivers’ real pay declined, volatility increased, and Uber’s profit margins rose sharply.
F42.claim: the joint Oxford–WIE analysis of 1.5 million trips (2016–2024) found that after dynamic pricing in 2023 real pay fell, volatility rose and Uber's margins rose sharply
F42.lineage: research: the Oxford audit and the TUC report

F43.quote: Under the system, two drivers performing identical trips can be paid vastly different amounts, with Uber keeping more than half of the fare in many cases.
F43.claim: identical trips can be paid very differently, Uber keeping more than half the fare in many cases
F43.lineage: dynamic pay: what changed for drivers

F44.quote: Worker Info Exchange (WIE) is an independent non‑profit organisation that helps platform workers turn their data into power. Founded in 2020, WIE works with drivers, couriers and trade‑union partners to:
F44.claim: WIE: an independent non-profit, founded in 2020, helping platform workers turn their data into power, with drivers, couriers and trade-union partners
F44.lineage: what it is: a non-profit helping workers turn the data collected from them at work into power

F45.quote: Secure workers’ right to access and understand the data that controls their work. … Investigate how algorithms determine pay, performance and job allocation. … Build data trusts so workers can combine and analyse their data collectively. … Support unions and grassroots organisations in using data for collective action, bargaining and transparency.
F45.claim: its four aims: data access, investigation of algorithms, data trusts, support for unions and grassroots organisations
F45.lineage: the three strands: data access, data investigations, data trusts

F46.quote: Uber's share of rider fares increased, to taking 29-50% from drivers according ...
F46.claim: a video: Uber's share of rider fares increased, to taking 29–50% from drivers, according to a source the truncated title does not show
F46.lineage: Uber's share of the fare (the video card)
F46.checked_against: the card's title (unreachable card; title only)

F47.quote: Digital rights are increasingly important in the fight for worker rights for gig workers who are managed and controlled at work by hidden algorithms. Opaque automated management systems foster exploitation and discrimination. They facilitate illegal workplace practices including unfair work allocation, performance management and dismissals.
F47.claim: gig workers are managed and controlled at work by hidden algorithms; opaque automated management systems foster exploitation and discrimination and facilitate illegal practices in work allocation, performance management and dismissals
F47.lineage: the problem it names: workers managed by hidden algorithms

F48.quote: Our solution is to help workers assert their digital rights under the law so that they may take control of their data, have full transparency of how they have been subject to algorithmic management and to challenge illegal or unfair automated management decisions.
F48.claim: its solution: workers asserting their digital rights under the law, to take control of their data, see how they were subject to algorithmic management and challenge automated management decisions
F48.lineage: the route: workers' digital rights under the law

F49.quote: We will do this by supporting trade unions and grassroots worker organisations to access and aggregate their data with other workers through the development of data trust(s). Armed with powerful analysis, workers can better monitor their conditions at work and take action to improve things whether on the streets, in the courts or in the legislature.
F49.claim: it will do this through data trusts with unions and grassroots organisations, so workers can act on the streets, in the courts or in the legislature
F49.lineage: the three strands: data access, data investigations, data trusts

F50.quote: Wikipedia does not have an article with this exact name.
F50.claim: Wikipedia has no article on Worker Info Exchange

F51.claim: Wikipedia's one statement of the entity, in another article, with a red link to its name: in July 2020 it joined IAATW and the ADCU in supporting Uber drivers' legal complaints for access to their personal data
